title: Gaussian surface area of a halfspace
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $a\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2=1$, and let $t\in\mathbb R$. The Gaussian surface area of the halfspace $\{z\in\mathbb R^n:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i z_i\le t\}$ is $\varphi(t)$, the standard Gaussian density at $t$.
hypotheses_covered: The squared coordinates of $a$ sum to $1$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. Write $P_\gamma(A)=\liminf_{t\to0^+}\bigl[\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(t)/t\bigr]_+$ in $[0,\infty]$, where $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$. For a vector $v\in\mathbb R^n$ with $\sum_i v_i^2=1$ and real $t$, the halfspace $H=\{z:\sum_i v_i z_i\le t\}$ satisfies $P_\gamma(H)=\varphi(t)$, where $\varphi(t)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-t^2/2}$.
